result.title: Can Visual World Models See Force?
result.summary: World models and vision-language-action policy models are increasingly proposed as foundations for robot manipulation. They predict how scenes evolve and which actions to take, yet successful manipulation depends not solely on following observable trajectories but also on the hidden variable of interaction force. Neurophysiology has shown that humans possess a visual prior for this hidden variable, motivating us to ask the question: Do the representations of visual foundation models also capture the forces involved in an interaction? We define force awareness as the ability of representations to (1) indicate when contact force is applied, (2) track how it changes during an interaction, and (3) reflect how large it is. We probe frozen image, video, world- and policy model representations with a lightweight readout trained on synchronized video and force measurements from two manipulation datasets. Our experiments show that most models capture when contact occurs but not how much force is being applied. Surprisingly, robot post-training does not improve this either, highlighting an important gap in current models capabilities.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用轻量读出探针，在同步视频与力测量数据上检验冻结的图像、视频、世界模型和策略模型表示是否编码接触力，结果发现多数模型只能指示接触是否发生，却无法跟踪或反映力的大小，机器人后训练也未改善。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作对「内部表示是否保留任务必要的隐藏物理变量」做了直接诊断，其「知何时、不知多大」的失败模式与探针范式可供核查 LVR 的 latent 状态是否同样只编码事件而不含连续量级信息。
